papers.title: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
papers.abstract: Harvest quadrature can change a discrete optimal control problem even when the state scheme stays fixed. We study this effect for a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. The difference appears in a model with harvesting alone: rewarding the scheme's removal flux gives a strictly convex reduced cost, whereas using prey density at the start of each step overestimates harvest and can create negative curvature and a strict local minimum that is not global. Rational root isolation certifies the two-step global minimizers. With diffusion in one space dimension, nonnegative bounded $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities, the costs, weighted gradients and Hessians differ by $O(\tau)$ uniformly in the spatial mesh, where $\tau$ is the time step. A uniform positive lower bound on the reduced Hessian gives the same order for the distance between nearby controls. A large enough effort penalty gives unique global discrete minimizers. We also prove positivity, exact population balance and a common variational limit, and derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions. Numerical tests trace changes in curvature and stationary controls across parameters and grids, with costs evaluated on a common reference using adaptive time stepping. The construction extends to weighted production--destruction systems, giving exact harvest accounting and smooth derivatives on fixed grids.

papers.title: Equilibrium measures for anisotropic exponential interaction energies with applications to transformers
papers.abstract: We study the minimization of anisotropic exponential interaction energies over probability measures on the sphere, motivated by mean-field models of self-attention in transformer architectures. For every symmetric positive definite interaction matrix, we relate the minimizer to a corresponding anisotropic Brownian motion and use the Feynman--Kac formula and elliptic regularity theory to show that it admits a smooth, strictly positive density on the sphere. We further show that it is the only stationary measure with full support for the dynamics considered. We use the stochastic viewpoint to derive an algorithm for sampling from the minimizer. In dimension two, we also propose a numerical scheme for approximating its density based on a Mathieu series expansion.

papers.title: Quantitative homogenization of Stokes flow in a perforated domain under low regularity of data and geometry
papers.abstract: We study the homogenization of the steady Stokes equations with no-slip conditions in a domain perforated by $\varepsilon$-periodic obstacles, whose limit is Darcy's law for the homogenized pressure $p^\ast$. We prove the quantitative error estimate with rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, natural in the presence of a boundary layer, only assuming that $f-\nabla p^\ast\in H^1$. Such estimates were previously available only under strong smoothness assumptions, such as $f\in C^{1,1/2}$. Our geometrical assumptions are also less stringent than in the previous analyses. The outer domain and the reference fluid cell need only be Lipschitz, the perforations may deviate from periodicity in a layer of width $O(\varepsilon)$ near the outer boundary, and the solid part may be connected (in three dimensions) and attached to the outer wall. In the absence of a boundary layer, the same argument yields the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ assuming only $f\in H^1$.

papers.title: Modified scattering and asymptotic completeness for a massive Dirac-wave system in dimension three
papers.abstract: We establish global well-posedness and modified scattering for the three-dimensional Dirac-Klein-Gordon system with a massive spinor and a massless scalar field, for small, sufficiently regular and localized initial data. This answers a question posed by Dong, Li, and Yuan in \cite[Case IV]{DLY23}. We also identify a Majorana-type condition on the initial data that yields linear scattering, showing that both linear and modified scattering solutions coexist in this model. Conversely, we establish asymptotic completeness for small asymptotic profiles satisfying suitable regularity and decay assumptions. The forward argument combines the hyperboloidal foliation method with testing by wave packets, whereas the backward construction relies on a contraction argument in suitably chosen norms.

papers.title: Blow-up profile decomposition and optimal Harnack inequalities for the $n$-Liouville equation
papers.abstract: We consider the problem $- \Delta_n u = h(x) e^u$ in a bounded domain $\Omega$ of $\mathbb R^n$, where $\Delta_n$ stands for the $n$-Laplacian and $h$ is a continuous function satisfying $0 < a \leq h \leq b$. Several new a priori estimates are obtained for the sets of solutions whose boundary oscillation is uniformly bounded by some constant. Those results are exploited to provide a profile decomposition in $L^\infty$-sense for a sequence of blowing-up solutions. We also present an optimal Harnack type inequality, which states that on a compact set $K \subset \Omega$ we have a universal estimate $\displaystyle \sup_K u + (n-1)\displaystyle \inf_{\Omega} u \leq C$.

papers.title: Leafwise thermalization near vacuum for the inhomogeneous Landau equation with very soft and Coulomb potentials
papers.abstract: We study the inhomogeneous Landau equation with very soft and Coulomb potentials, $\gamma\in[-3,-2]$, for data near vacuum. Unlike for $\gamma>-2$, the collisions along a free trajectory have a divergent time integral, so the dynamics is not a perturbation of free transport. It is instead organized along \emph{leaves}, the velocity distributions in the variable $z=x-tv$: on each leaf the solution follows a homogeneous Landau flow with a leaf-dependent collision rate, first far from equilibrium and then near a Maxwellian whose parameters approximately solve a compressible Euler system with the free-expansion prefactor $t^{-2}$. For data of size $\epsilon$, analytic in velocity and Gaussian in space, we prove global existence of classical solutions, relaxation of every leaf (not uniform in $x/t$), and convergence of the leaf parameters at rate $t^{-1}$. The solution scatters in $L^1$ to the free transport of a thermalized profile that generally remains at a fixed relative distance from the data. The $L^1$ distance to the scattering state decays like $(1+\epsilon\log t)^{-(p-3)/p}$ at $\gamma=-2$ and $(1+\epsilon t^{|\gamma|-2})^{-(p-3)/p}$ for $\gamma<-2$, where $\langle v\rangle^{-p}$ is the velocity decay of the data; these rates are sharp when the spatial profiles stay away from Maxwellians. Each leaf relaxes on its own clock: as a power of $t$ proportional to its collision rate at $\gamma=-2$, and as a stretched exponential of its clock for $\gamma<-2$. We also prove the near-Maxwellian and homogeneous results we need beyond the literature, including at $\gamma=-2$.

Moreover, we show that an analogous approximation theorem is not viable for the Dirichlet-Regularity problem, nor for the variational Dirichlet problem. All of the results are new even in the case of the Laplacian and on the unit ball.

papers.title: Regularity of Solutions to Non-Local Equations on Homogeneous Groups
papers.abstract: We prove a Harnack inequality and H\"older continuity of solutions to non-linear nonlocal equations on homogeneous groups. In addition, we show basic properties of the involved Sobolev spaces, which are crucial for the analysis of such operators.

papers.title: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
papers.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_\tau:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z\tau)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_{\tau}(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_{\tau}$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given.

papers.title: Stokes Waves in a Finite-Depth Fluid via a Conformal Transformation
papers.abstract: Euler equations for a spatially periodic surface in a two-dimensional fluid of a finite depth are reduced to a system of evolution equations after a conformal transformation. Compared to the previously developed formal approach, we show that the system of evolution equations is complemented by two constraints which determine the new depth in conformal variables and the Bernoulli integration constant. A locally unique continuation of the traveling Stokes waves with respect to the wave speed is studied by using arguments based on the implicit function theorem. We show that the constraints on the traveling wave profile recover the correct small-amplitude expansion of Stokes waves in physical variables. We also prove for the co-periodic stability problem that the real unstable eigenvalues may bifurcate from the zero eigenvalue only at a critical point of the wave energy. Finally, we perform numerical approximations of the wave profiles for both small and large amplitudes and illustrate different bifurcations along the solution family.

papers.title: On the Flucher--Rumpf isoperimetric question for the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem: a conformal reformulation, quantitative bounds and the second variation at the disc
papers.abstract: Let $c(\Omega)$ be the Bernoulli constant of a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\R^N$, that is, the infimum of the parameters $\lambda$ for which the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem $\Delta u=0$ in $\Omega\setminus K$, $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, $u=1$ and $|\nabla u|=\lambda$ on $\partial K$ admits a classical solution. Flucher and Rumpf asked whether $c(\Omega)\ge c(\Omega^*)$, where $\Omega^*$ is the ball of the same volume. The variational analogue was settled by Daners and Kawohl, but the variational constant differs from $c$ already for the ball, and the original question remains open. We prove the following. (i) Through a conformal parametrisation of $\Omega\setminus K$ by an annulus, every classical solution in a simply connected planar domain with connected, filled free set satisfies $\lambda\ge\mu/R$, where $\pi R^2=|\Omega|$ and $\mu\approx 2.485268$; hence $c(\Omega)\ge 0.9142\,c(\Omega^*)$ for every bounded planar convex domain of class $C^1$. (ii) In this class, the Flucher--Rumpf inequality is equivalent to an area inequality for analytic functions in an annulus, which also provides an explicit generator of exact solutions. (iii) A Rellich--Pohozaev identity yields, in every dimension $N\ge2$ and for every strictly star-shaped domain, $c(\Omega)\ge\max\{\sqrt{\theta(\Omega)},\kappa_N\}\,c(\Omega^*)$, where $\theta(\Omega)\in(0,1]$ is an explicit geometric quantity equal to $1$ only for balls and $\kappa_N$ is an explicit constant with $\kappa_3\approx0.650$ and $\kappa_N\to1$ as $N\to\infty$.

papers.title: Stability of Self-Similar Expansions for Self-Gravitating Hyperelastic Bodies
papers.abstract: We consider the three-dimensional elastodynamics system with nonlocal gravitational coupling and nonlinear traction-free boundary conditions, modeling an isolated self-gravitating hyperelastic body, where the strain-energy function is assumed to be objective, isotropic, and homogeneous of degree $-1$. We prove nonlinear stability of a self-similarly expanding separable solution, recently constructed by the authors [JangLeslie2025], under radial perturbations satisfying the codimension-one constraint of zero total energy. Using a self-similar reformulation analogous to that developed for the mass-critical Euler--Poisson system in [HadzicJang2018CPAM], we recast the perturbed equation as a scalar nonlinear five-dimensional radial wave equation and the nonlinear traction-free boundary condition as a homogeneous Neumann condition. A key is to identify a quasilinear form of the leading-order spatial operator that is compatible with this boundary condition and yields coercive energy estimates. Our energy estimates capture the stabilizing effect of the background expansion and yield global existence and nonlinear codimension-one stability in self-similar variables.

papers.title: Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear Kirchhoff equation on the waveguide manifolds $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n$: \begin{align*} -\left( a+b \int_{\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n}|\nabla_{x,y}u(x,y)|^2\,dxdy\right) \Delta_{x,y}u+\omega u=|u|^\alpha u, \end{align*} where $a,b>0$, $\omega\in \mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\in(0,2^*)$. We first establish existence of the normalized ground states when $\alpha\in(0,2^*)$. To precisely characterize the $y$-dependence of ground states, we apply a scaling argument to handle the integral term $ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}^n} |\nabla_{x,y} u(x,y)|^2 dxdy$. To this end, we construct two distinct modified energy functionals, through which we establish the $y$-independence and $y$-dependence of the ground states in two specific regimes: $(i)$ $ d + n \leq 4$ and $\alpha \in (0, \frac{8}{d+n})$; $(ii)$ $d = n = 1$ and $\alpha \in (8, \infty)$.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

papers.title: Global dynamics and the diffusive limit of the one-species non-cutoff Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system
papers.abstract: The rigorous derivation of incompressible plasma equations from kinetic plasma models is a fundamental problem in kinetic theory. For the one-species Vlasov--Maxwell--Boltzmann system without angular cutoff, global well-posedness and the diffusive limit have remained largely open in the soft-potential regime. We resolve both problems for $0<s<1$ and $\max\{-3,-\frac32-2s\}<\gamma<-2s$. For sufficiently small initial perturbations, we construct unique global classical solutions with energy and time-decay estimates uniform in the Knudsen number $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$. The key analytical contribution is a family of coercivity and trilinear estimates for the non-cutoff collision operators with time-dependent quadratic exponential velocity weights. Exploiting conservation of energy in collisions, these estimates combine with weighted interpolation to control the high-order electromagnetic terms despite the slow decay of the electric field. For well-prepared initial data, we prove strong convergence to the incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier--Maxwell system as $\varepsilon\to0$.

papers.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.

papers.title: Lipschitz bounds and gradient continuity for the Trudinger equation
papers.abstract: We establish local spatial Lipschitz and gradient H\"older estimates for general nonnegative weak solutions to Trudinger's equation $\partial_t u^{p-1}=\Delta_pu$, $p>1$. The estimates are uniform across the zero set. The proofs combine Bernstein-type estimates for power transformations, smooth approximation, and comparison with exponential barriers near the zero set.

papers.title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Positive Bounded Solutions for Semilinear Dirichlet Problems in Exterior-Star Domains
papers.abstract: We prove the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive bounded solutions for the Dirichlet problem $$-\Delta u=f(u)\,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \Omega, \ \ u=0\,\ \ \text{on}\ \ \partial\Omega,$$ where $f$ is a positive reaction and $\Omega\subsetneq\mathbb{R}^d$ is a uniformly $C^{2,\gamma}$ domain with a star-shaped complement. Our uniqueness result gives a positive answer to Open Question 1 of [H. Berestycki and C. Graham, ARMA, 2026].

papers.title: On the nodal set of the second eigenfunction of the Laplacian in convex domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$. We prove that the closure of the interior nodal set of any second Dirichlet eigenfunction of $\Omega$ intersects $\partial\Omega$. The proof combines the ground-state derivative and the quantitative log-concavity estimate of Andrews and Clutterbuck with a variational argument.

papers.title: A Liouville theorem for L\'evy operators on nilpotent and compact Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a left-invariant L\'evy operator, with characteristics $(a,b,\mu)$, on a connected and simply connected Lie group $G$ that is either compact or nilpotent with $[G,[G,G]]$ relatively compact (equivalently, of step at most two). We prove that every bounded distributional solution of $\mathcal{L}u=0$ is right-invariant under the closed subgroup $P=\overline{\langle\exp\mathfrak h_0\cup\text{supp}\mu\rangle}$, where $\mathfrak h_0=\text{Lie}\langle b,\operatorname{ran}(a)\rangle$, and is constant if and only if $P=G$. In the compact case we give three proofs, one through the It\^o--Kawada equidistribution theorem, one by propagation of the maximum and one by an application of the Peter-Weyl theorem, while the nilpotent case rests on the Choquet--Deny theorem of B\'enard and Frisch.

papers.title: Smoothing of the Coupled KdV System on \mathbb{T}
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear smoothing properties of the Coupled KdV system posed on the torus. This system arises as a particular case of the four-parameter family of Boussinesq systems studied by Bona, Chen and Saut, corresponding to the choice $\eta^{2}=\frac{2}{3}$, $b=d=0$ and $a=c=\frac{1}{6}$. Although the similarities with the periodic KdV equation and the favorable resonance structure of the Majda-Biello system for the coupling parameter $\alpha =-1$ might suggest that smoothing can be established by a relatively straightforward adaptation of existing techniques, the nonlinear interactions in the Coupled KdV system introduce additional difficulties. In particular, certain mixed interactions lead to degeneracies in the associated resonance functions, resulting in a loss of frequency decay that restricts the attainable smoothing gain. By combining normal-form reductions, duality arguments and Bourgain-space estimates, we establish a smoothing gain of any order $ a< \min \{1,\frac{2}{3}(2s+1)\} $ for $s>-\frac{1}{2}$. Our result demonstrates that the interplay between nonlinear interactions and resonance structures plays a decisive role in determining the smoothing properties of coupled dispersive systems.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for $\sigma$-evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients via upper decay indicators
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first main goal is to investigate the Cauchy problem for the linear $\sigma$-evolution equation $$u_{tt}+a^2(t)(-\Delta)^\sigma u+b(t)u_t+m^2(t)u=0, $$ where propagation speed, damping term and mass are time-dependent functions. Under suitable assumptions on the interaction among these coefficients, we not only derive decay estimates for the solution and its derivatives in terms of the effective parabolic time scale $\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(s,t):=\int_s^t a^2(\tau)/b(\tau) d\tau$, but also conclude the additional decay induced by the mass term and the upper decay indicators of the initial data. Especially, one can recognize that the time-derivative estimate for solutions exhibits a competition between $m^2(t)$ and $a^2(t)\left(1+\mathcal{V}_{a,b}(0,t)\right)^{-1}$. For the corresponding semi-linear problem with the nonlinear term $|u|^p$, we also establish global (in time) existence of small data solutions fulfilling decay estimates, coming from the mass factor $\exp\left(-\int_0^t m^2(\tau)/b(\tau)d\tau\right)$, under the same assumptions on these coefficients.

papers.title: Weak-type $(p,p)$ inequalities for Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: For $1\le p\le2$, we obtain the sharp weak-type $(p,p)$ inequality for each classical Riesz transform on real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^n$, with the same optimal constant as for the Hilbert transform. The proof combines the Bellman function method of \cite{BHV} with Janakiraman's sharp strip potential \cite{Janakiraman}.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Strichartz estimates for general irrotational compressible Euler backgrounds and positive estimates for a spherical isotropic background solution
papers.abstract: We consider the free boundary problem for the irrotational compressible Euler equation in a physical vacuum setting. By using the irrotationality condition in the Eulerian formulation of Ifrim and Tataru, we previously showed that the problem can be rephrased in terms of the velocity potential function as an acoustic wave equation that turns out to be widely used in solar seismology. This paper is another step towards understanding what Strichartz estimates are achievable for the aforementioned equation. Our object of study is the corresponding linearized problem. In a previous work, we constructed a class of gallery modes in a model stationary case, which turned out to be counterexamples to Strichartz estimates, forcing a loss of derivatives. By a careful regularization of the domain defining function, we transplant these counterexamples to general Euler backgrounds, and obtain general counterexamples in the same range. On the other hand, we also prove that for the background corresponding to a concrete affine isotropic spherical solution for the irrotational compressible Euler equations, one has Strichartz estimates up to the aforementioned threshold, which shows that they are optimal for at least some explicit Euler backgrounds. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first results of this kind for explicit solutions of the irrotational compressible Euler equations in a physical vacuum.

papers.title: Minimal time of null-controllability of the multi-dimensional singular Grushin equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the null-controllability of the multi-dimensional Grushin equation with an inverse-square potential on cylinders. In the critically degenerate case, we compute the minimal time of null-controllability from vertical strips, obtaining an explicit formula depending on the distance of the strip to the singular set and on the strength of the singular potential. To do so, after a Fourier and spherical harmonic decomposition of our control system, we use the moments method for radial problems to construct controls on annuli. For this purpose, we prove a uniform spectral gap and uniform localization estimates for the eigenfunctions of the infinite family of radial operators that arise. We then reduce the control zone using spectral inequalities and the Lebeau-Robbiano method. In the weakly degenerate case, we prove null-controllability in arbitrarily small time from any open set. This is done using the transmutation method and quantitative observability estimates for radial waves, which yield a cost of null-controllability from annuli for the Fourier components of our system that is uniform with respect to the frequency. We conclude again with spectral inequalities and the Lebeau-Robbiano method.

papers.title: Boundary regularity, finiteness and stability of energy-maximizing vortex patches
papers.abstract: We establish boundary regularity for energy-maximizing vortex patches of the 2-D incompressible Euler equations in a bounded Jordan domain. These results resolve Turkington's free-boundary regularity question throughout the full range of admissible parameters. For bounded convex domains, we further prove that the set of energy maximizers is finite at each prescribed patch area. When the domain is smooth, the number of maximizers is uniformly bounded over all admissible patch areas, and every maximizer is Lyapunov stable in $L^p$ for any $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: On Minima of 3D Lennard-Jones Lattice Energy and FCC-Tetragonal-Simple Hexagonal Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Denote the Epstein zeta function by \begin{equation}\label{eq:Epstein} E(L,s):=\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}}|v|^{-2s}, \;\;\hbox{where}\;\;L\;\;\hbox{is a lattice}; \qquad s>\frac32. \end{equation} We consider the three-dimensional Lennard--Jones lattice energy, which has the form \[ \mathcal E(L)=\frac12E(L,6)-E(L,3). \] We completely classify the minimizers at every covolume $|L|$, and we prove that as the covolume increases, the minimizing phase changes from the FCC to the body-centered tetragonal and then to the simple-hexagonal lattice. Thereby, we give a positive answer to an open problem raised by Blanc--Lewin [EMS Survey Series 2015, Section~2.5,~(27), pp.~268--269] and B\'etermin--Petrache [JMP 2017, Question~1.15], and we prove and clarify the conjecture of B\'etermin--\v{S}amaj--Trav\v{e}nec [SAM 2023].

papers.title: Behavior of the Caputo time fractional equations as the order $\alpha\rightarrow 0^+$: the resolvent limit and its stochastic interpretation
papers.abstract: We study the behavior, as the fractional order $\alpha\rightarrow0^+$, of the Caputo time derivative and of the solutions of $D_t^\alpha u=Au$ in a Banach space. The solutions converge for every $t>0$ to the time-independent resolvent value $(1-A)^{-1}\phi$. A single bounded fractional resolvent family already forces the sectoriality of $A$ and yields operator-norm convergence with rate $O(\alpha)$ and a full expansion in powers of $\alpha$. The engine is an expansion of the Mittag-Leffler function in its order, $E_\alpha(z)=(1-z)^{-1}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}c_k\alpha^k\mathrm{Li}_{-k}(z)+O(\alpha^{K+1})$ on sectors away from $[1,\infty)$, the corresponding qualitative limit going back to Mittag-Leffler's summability of the geometric series. We also develop stochastic interpretations using inverse $\alpha$-stable subordinators, and establish connections with probabilistic potential theory, the Feynman--Kac formula, and degenerate elliptic equations.

papers.title: Optimal first order global regularity for fractional harmonic maps into spheres
papers.abstract: This paper is a continuation of our previous work on global regularity theory for the sphere-valued fractional harmonic maps which was initialized by several authors such as Millot-Pegon-Schikorra and Millot-Sire. By adapting the powerful quantitative stratification approach developed by Naber-Valtorta on harmonic mappings, we establish a corresponding stratification theory for fractional harmonic maps, from which an optimal first order global regularity theory and the rectifiable structure of singular sets follow.

papers.title: Antisymmetry Breaking for Critical Poincar\'e-Sobolev Extremals in the Three Dimensional Ball
papers.abstract: We study extremal functions for Poincar\'e-Sobolev inequalities in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$. At the critical exponent $q=6$, we prove that no minimizer is antisymmetric with respect to any hyperplane through the origin. We obtain a positive gap between the general and antisymmetric optimal constants. Continuity of these constants yields antisymmetry breaking for exponents sufficiently close to $6$. We introduce two critical indices to describe the onset of antisymmetry breaking and prove that global minimizers are antisymmetric at both indices.
